identifier the package must carry as a declared resource, and no

TestMailRequest.description:
One administrator-triggered SMTP test.

``idempotency_key`` identifies the test operation, not the configuration:
a retry of the same request reuses the key and replays its intent, while
a new test — after a failure, a configuration change or simply again —
carries a new key and starts a new send. The key is persisted as declared
inside the test source's own scope, so this bound is the stored one.
TestMailRequest.title: TestMailRequest

post.description: Create one pending invitation and register its mail in the same transaction.
Accept one invitation with its token; no session exists before acceptance.
Resend with a freshly rotated token; the delivered code stops working.
Register one delegated send; the source comes from the verified call.
Confirm the real outcome of one unconfirmed send; it is never re-sent.

Register one administrator-triggered test mail for durable delivery.

The idempotency key is the client's operation key: retrying the same
request replays its intent, while a new test — after a failed send, a
configuration change or simply another attempt — carries a new key and
starts a new delivery. The configuration revision deliberately plays no
part: an unchanged configuration must not turn a fresh test into a stale
replay of an older outcome. The key is stored as declared because the
mail source scope already namespaces it, so the published length bound
and the persisted one are the same.
